question.worked_solution:
The sum to infinity ${S}_{\infty }$ of a geometric series is given by

$$
{S}_{\infty }=\frac{{a}_{1}}{1-r},\,|r|<1.
$$

The first term is 

$$
{a}_{1}=\frac{9}{4}{(-\frac{1}{3})}^{2(1)}=\frac{9}{4}{(-\frac{1}{3})}^{2}
$$

 

and the second term is 

$$
{a}_{2}=\frac{9}{4}{(-\frac{1}{3})}^{2(2)}=\frac{9}{4}{(-\frac{1}{3})}^{4}.
$$

Therefore, the common ratio is 

$$
r=\frac{{a}_{2}}{{a}_{1}}=\frac{\frac{9}{4}{(-\frac{1}{3})}^{4}}{\frac{9}{4}{(-\frac{1}{3})}^{2}}={(-\frac{1}{3})}^{2}=\frac{1}{9}.
$$

 

So, the sum of the series is

$$
\begin{aligned}{\sum }_{n=1}^{\infty }\frac{9}{4}{(-\frac{1}{3})}^{2n} & =\frac{{a}_{1}}{1-r} \\  & =\frac{\frac{9}{4}(\frac{1}{9})}{(1-\frac{1}{9})} \\  & =\frac{(\frac{1}{4})}{(\frac{8}{9})} \\  & =\frac{1}{4}\cdot \frac{9}{8} \\  & =\frac{9}{32}.\end{aligned}
$$
